meter: USB power meter feeding the board's native USB port, through the meter's USB-A port (its USB-C port reads about 20 % more on this board only: the lower reading is used); display V, A, mAh, Wh; read by eye
method: each phase 600 s; energy = meter mAh x volts x 3.6 J, after subtracting the idle rate (19 mAh / 600 s) for the seconds the meter timer ran past 600 s; per inference = energy / runs; above idle = (mAh - 19 x seconds / 600) x volts x 3.6 / runs; the meter counts whole mAh (+-1 mAh per reading); one run per phase (no seeds, no repeats)
tools: tools/energy_loop.py (firmware: 0xE5 / TFLite loop on the first input, 'L:count,elapsed_us,class')

symbex.label: SYMBEX runs/sizing/h128_512_s42, standard engine, lut16, flash; exact against its simulation on the chip, 100 %

idle.label: idle, measured Nov 14 on the same board and meter port (cnn_cifar_resnet8 ENERGY.md)

tflite.label: TFLite Micro INT8, runs/tflite/fashion_int8_h128_512.tflite (same shape, INT8 QAT), ESP-NN, flash

notes: Accuracy differs: binary 87.5 % against INT8 QAT 89.8 % (same shape, labels only, 3 seeds; README).
A first SYMBEX weights-in-RAM run was read 380 s late (46 mAh at timer 16:20): discarded and repeated.

weights_in_ram.question: does TFLite draw less power in flash because it waits on the flash? (weights in RAM for both)

symbex_ram.label: SYMBEX, same model, weights in RAM

tflite_ram.label: TFLite Micro INT8, same model, weights in RAM (fashion_tflite.py --model-ram)

weights_in_ram.answer: not supported: with weights in RAM both draw MORE power (TFLite 0.69 -> 0.77 W, SYMBEX 0.77 -> 0.91 W at the same 0.415 ms); the cause is not measured
